cases.claim: Language-specific conventions: Python uses snake_case (vars/functions), PascalCase (classes), UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (constants), is_ boolean prefix
cases.prompt:
This is Python code. Review the names and rename each to follow standard Python naming conventions, giving a one-line rationale per change.

```python
DEFAULT_retries = 3

class userAccount:
    def GetUserData(self, UserId):
        active = UserId > 0
        maxItems = 50
        return active
```
cases.rubric:
Grade ONLY on correct application of Python-specific casing as documented by the skill: function `GetUserData` -> snake_case `get_user_data`; parameter/local `UserId` -> `user_id`, `maxItems` -> `max_items`; class `userAccount` -> PascalCase `UserAccount`; module constant `DEFAULT_retries` -> UPPER_SNAKE_CASE `DEFAULT_RETRIES`; boolean `active` -> `is_active` (Python is_ prefix). 

CAP: If the response applies JavaScript camelCase to Python variables/functions (e.g. leaves `getUserData`/`maxItems` in camelCase) or otherwise does not convert methods/vars to snake_case, cap at 0.3. Subtract ~0.2 for each distinct error: class not PascalCase; constant not UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; any function/variable left in camelCase or PascalCase; boolean `active` not given an is_/has_/can_ prefix.

SCORING ANCHOR (apply strictly): a fully correct response that fixes every name to the right Python case (snake_case funcs/vars, PascalCase class, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constant, is_ boolean) scores 0.80. Award 0.81-0.90 only if it is ALSO exemplary, e.g. it correctly distinguishes the module-level constant from ordinary locals and names each convention explicitly. Award 0.91-1.00 only if flawless AND exceptional in every respect (rare).

cases.claim: Go conventions: acronyms are All caps (HTTPServer, not HttpServer); exported PascalCase, unexported camelCase
cases.rubric:
Grade ONLY on Go's acronym-casing convention as documented by the skill (acronyms all caps: HTTPServer not HttpServer), plus exported/unexported casing. Expected: exported type `HttpServer` -> `HTTPServer`; exported method `FetchJson` -> `FetchJSON`; unexported field `apiUrl` -> `apiURL` (stays unexported camelCase but the URL acronym is all caps). 

CAP: If the response leaves acronyms in mixed case (Http/Json/Url) or 'corrects' them the wrong way (e.g. `HttpServer` unchanged, or `FetchJson` -> `fetchJson`), cap at 0.3. Subtract ~0.2 for each distinct error: `HttpServer` not made `HTTPServer`; `FetchJson` not made `FetchJSON`; `apiUrl` not made `apiURL`; changing the exported/unexported status incorrectly (e.g. capitalising the unexported field to `APIURL`/`ApiUrl`, or lower-casing the exported type/method).

SCORING ANCHOR (apply strictly): a fully correct response that all-caps every acronym while preserving each identifier's exported/unexported first-letter casing scores 0.80. Award 0.81-0.90 only if it is ALSO exemplary, e.g. it explicitly explains WHY the field stays lowercase-initial (unexported) while its acronym is still uppercased.
